title: Architectural approach for Interactive 3D Retro-Tech Landing Page
context: The project requires a high-performance 3D environment featuring specific retro-aesthetic effects (wireframes, neon glows, and scanlines). A robust 3D engine is necessary to handle the 3D geometry and rotation logic while maintaining a smooth frame rate for the 'Cyber-Grid' visual style.
decision: Utilize Three.js as the primary 3D engine to render the wireframe model and handle the Y-axis rotation. Implement 'Cyber-Grid' effects (neon cyan, glowing vertices) using custom ShaderMaterials. A 2D CSS/Canvas overlay will be used for the CRT scanline effect and the glassmorphic UI components to decouple the 3D scene logic from the UI layer.
alternativesConsidered: Raw WebGL (Rejected due to high complexity and significant development overhead for basic scene management)
Babylon.js (Rejected as Three.js provides a more extensive ecosystem for wireframe-specific shaders and neon-style post-processing)

positive: Decoupled UI and 3D logic allows for easier maintenance of the glassmorphic elements
Consistent performance across modern browsers using standard WebGL
negative: Increased initial bundle size due to the inclusion of the Three.js library
risks: Potential frame-rate drops on low-end mobile devices when rendering complex shader effects
Potential issues with 'glitch' effect synchronization across different browser refresh rates
